questions.prompt: Explain how the unit circle defines cos t and sin t for every real number t.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain how the unit circle defines cos t and sin t for every real number t.
questions.correct_answer: Start at (1, 0) and travel |t| units along the unit circle, counterclockwise if t > 0 and clockwise if t < 0; the endpoint is (cos t, sin t).
questions.required_method: Describe the arc, the endpoint, and the coordinates.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: arc of length |t|, direction by sign, coordinates of the endpoint.

questions.prompt: Explain why sin(t + 2π) = sin t for every real number t.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why sin(t + 2π) = sin t for every real number t.
questions.correct_answer: Adding 2π adds one full trip around the circle, so t + 2π ends at the same point as t and has the same y-coordinate.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: 2π is the circumference; same endpoint; same coordinate.
